prompt_md: A knight stands on a corner square of a chessboard. What's the fewest knight moves it needs to reach the square diagonally next to it?
prompt_short: Knight in a corner. Fewest moves to the diagonally adjacent square?
hint_md: From a corner, a knight has only two moves, and both lead away.
explain_intuition_md: In the middle of the board, 2 moves can take a knight one square diagonally. From a corner, both of those 2-move routes step off the edge. A knight always needs an even number of moves to reach a square of its own color, so the next best is 4.
explain_math_md: Searching every route from $a1$: $b2$ is first reached after $4$ moves (for example $a1 \to c2 \to e3 \to c4 \to b2$).
